questions.prompt: Name the energy store that increases when an object is lifted upwards.
questions.answer: Gravitational potential energy store.

questions.prompt: State the energy store that a stretched spring has.
questions.answer: Elastic potential energy store.

questions.prompt: Name the energy store that decreases when a fuel is burned.
questions.answer: Chemical energy store.

questions.prompt: Define a system.
questions.answer: An object or group of objects.

questions.prompt: State the unit of kinetic energy.
questions.answer: The joule (J).

questions.prompt: Name the energy store that a moving object has.
questions.answer: Kinetic energy store.

questions.prompt: State the unit of spring constant.
questions.answer: Newtons per metre (N/m).

title: Change in thermal energy and specific heat capacity

questions.prompt: Define specific heat capacity.
questions.answer: The energy required to raise the temperature of 1 kg of a substance by 1 °C.

questions.prompt: State the unit of specific heat capacity.
questions.answer: J/kg °C (joules per kilogram per degree Celsius).

questions.prompt: State three things that the increase in temperature of a heated system depends on.
questions.answer: The mass of the substance heated, the type of material (its specific heat capacity) and the energy input to the system.

questions.prompt: Define power.
questions.answer: The rate at which energy is transferred, or the rate at which work is done.

questions.prompt: State the power of a device that transfers 1 joule of energy every second.
questions.answer: 1 watt (W).

questions.prompt: State the principle of conservation of energy.
questions.answer: Energy can be transferred usefully, stored or dissipated, but cannot be created or destroyed.

questions.prompt: Define what is meant by energy being 'dissipated'.
questions.answer: Energy is transferred to the surroundings in less useful ways (stored in less useful stores), so it is wasted.

questions.prompt: Name the energy store that wasted energy is usually transferred to.
questions.answer: The thermal energy store of the surroundings.

questions.prompt: Name a way of reducing unwanted energy transfers caused by friction.
questions.answer: Lubrication (e.g. oil or grease).

questions.prompt: State how increasing the thermal conductivity of a wall material affects the rate of energy transfer through it.
questions.answer: It increases the rate of energy transfer by conduction.

questions.prompt: State how increasing the thickness of a building's walls affects the rate at which the building cools.
questions.answer: It slows the rate of cooling (reduces the rate of energy transfer).

questions.prompt: Define thermal conductivity.
questions.answer: The rate at which thermal energy is conducted through a material.

questions.prompt: Calculate the efficiency of a device that receives 200 J of energy and usefully transfers 150 J.
Define efficiency.
questions.answer: The proportion of the total input energy transfer that is usefully transferred (useful output energy transfer ÷ total input energy transfer).

questions.prompt: Define 'renewable energy resource'.
questions.answer: An energy resource that is being (or can be) replenished as it is used.

questions.prompt: State two renewable energy resources.
questions.answer: Any two of: wind, solar, hydroelectric, tides, waves, geothermal, bio-fuel.

questions.prompt: State two non-renewable energy resources.
questions.answer: Any two of: coal, oil, gas (fossil fuels), nuclear fuel.

questions.prompt: Define 'non-renewable energy resource'.
questions.answer: An energy resource that is not being replenished as it is used (it will run out).

questions.prompt: Name one energy resource whose output depends on the weather.
questions.answer: Wind, solar or wave power (any one).

questions.prompt: State one environmental impact of burning fossil fuels.
questions.answer: It releases carbon dioxide, which contributes to global warming (sulfur dioxide released causes acid rain).

questions.prompt: State why nuclear fuel is classed as a non-renewable energy resource.
questions.answer: It is not replenished as it is used.
